title: China's Most Intricate Art Is Sculpted From Butter — Kumbum, Qinghai | China Travel Expert
description:
China's most intricate temple art is sculpted from yak butter — and every year it melts and is made again.

At Kumbum Monastery (Ta'er Si) in Qinghai, monks shape butter into flowers, animals and Buddhist scenes, carving in freezing rooms with ice-chilled hands so the body's heat won't soften it. These "butter flowers" (酥油花) are one of the monastery's Three Arts, alongside appliqué and murals. Founded in 1583 at the birthplace of Tsongkhapa — founder of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism — Kumbum is one of the six great Gelug monasteries. The name means "100,000 enlightening bodies of the Buddha."

This is stop one on the Qinghai-Gansu loop — an expert-led, at-your-pace route where Kumbum's altitude eases you in before the lakes and grasslands ahead.

🧭 Expert Tip: Begin the loop here and take it slow — starting at Kumbum lets you acclimate to the altitude before the higher stops, and it's worth timing your visit to the butter-sculpture display.
